items.title: Jack Sheldon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: And then Charlie Parker came out and I got to play with him. We were playing at a place called Dingbods on Florence and Normandy.

ctx.x: Yeah. So it wasn’t purely just the music. It was the whole spectrum.

The acceptance. Yeah, being in front of an audience and getting the reaction from the people, I guess getting that love, and wanting that love and wanting to play. I was always lucky, I always got to hang around with the greatest musicians of the time. Down in Florida, now when I was started, well Ross Tompkins was a little after me, and he was © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

down there, and there were some — Bobby Banks, he was an alto player that was in Jacksonville, Florida, and he introduced me to Charlie Parker, which sounded strange to me at first, very strange. And Dizzy Gillespie sounded strange to me then too. I liked Al Killian and Roy Eldridge and Coleman Hawkins and those guys.
